sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: It's almost that time for the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 奥运会的时间快到了。

sentences.en: The pageantry, the dreams, breathtaking victories.
sentences.zh: 盛大的场面、梦想、令人屏息的胜利。

sentences.en: For fans, it's an event of extraordinary drama.
sentences.zh: 对于粉丝来说，这是一场充满非凡戏剧性的盛事。

sentences.en: Athletes from across the globe competing at the very highest level,
sentences.zh: 来自全球各地的运动员在最高水平上竞技，

sentences.en: at the limits of human endurance.
sentences.zh: 挑战人类耐力的极限。

sentences.en: Social scientists find the Games equally compelling
sentences.zh: 社会科学家们发现奥运会同样引人入胜，

sentences.en: for what they reveal about human behavior.
sentences.zh: 因为它揭示了人类行为的奥秘。

sentences.en: When a match ends, the winners and losers do something
sentences.zh: 当比赛结束时，胜者和败者会做出某种反应，

sentences.en: that's immediate, automatic, it's unconscious,
sentences.zh: 这种反应是即时的、自动的、无意识的，

sentences.en: they have no control of it, it just happens.
sentences.zh: 他们无法控制，它就这样发生了。

sentences.en: About a second later, then they come to their senses
sentences.zh: 大约一秒钟后，他们回过神来，

sentences.en: and they realize that they're on stage.
sentences.zh: 意识到自己正处于聚光灯下。

sentences.en: And whatever rules they've learned to manage their expressions kick in then.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们学会的那些用来管理表情的规则便开始发挥作用。

sentences.en: Coming up, what the Olympics can teach us about human behavior
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将探讨奥运会能教会我们哪些关于人类行为的知识，

sentences.en: from a professor who's also an Olympic judo coach.
sentences.zh: 嘉宾是一位同时担任奥运柔道教练的心理学教授。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: My guest today is David Matsumoto.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是戴维·松本。

sentences.en: He's a professor of psychology at San Francisco State University.
sentences.zh: 他是旧金山州立大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He's used the Olympics as a laboratory for psychological observations.
sentences.zh: 他将奥运会作为心理学观察的实验室。

sentences.en: But he's also been a part of the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 但他本人也曾是奥运会的一员。

sentences.en: David's coached the U.S.
sentences.zh: 戴维曾担任美国

sentences.en: Olympic judo team,
sentences.zh: 奥运柔道队的教练，

sentences.en: and his daughter has competed in the Games.
sentences.zh: 他的女儿也曾参加过奥运会。

sentences.en: I'm going to talk to him today first about his research,
sentences.zh: 今天我首先要和他谈谈他的研究，

sentences.en: and then about what a sharp-eyed psychologist
sentences.zh: 然后探讨一位敏锐的心理学家

sentences.en: might observe about human behavior at the Games.
sentences.zh: 在奥运会上能观察到哪些人类行为。

sentences.en: David, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 戴维，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我参加。

sentences.en: You photographed 84 athletes from 34 countries
sentences.zh: 你拍摄了来自34个国家的84名运动员，

sentences.en: who were competing in the 2004 Athens Olympics judo competitions,
sentences.zh: 他们参加了2004年雅典奥运会的柔道比赛，

sentences.en: and you photographed them at the moments when they won or lost their matches.
sentences.zh: 你在他们赢得或输掉比赛的瞬间拍摄了他们。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, what you find is that people all around the world
sentences.zh: 嗯，你发现世界各地的人们，

sentences.en: show exactly the same types of expressions depending upon whether they won or loSt.
sentences.zh: 无论胜负，都会表现出完全相同的表情类型。

sentences.en: So those who won a match or won a medal, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，那些赢得比赛或获得奖牌的人，

sentences.en: invariably showed some kind of enjoyment, smile.
sentences.zh: 总是会表现出某种愉悦或微笑。

sentences.en: And those who lost the last match showed nothing sometimes.
sentences.zh: 而那些输掉最后一场比赛的人，有时则毫无表情。

sentences.en: Some of them showed sadness.
sentences.zh: 有些人表现出悲伤。

sentences.en: Some of them showed some kind of distress.
sentences.zh: 有些人表现出某种痛苦。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing about these findings is that
sentences.zh: 但这些发现有趣的地方在于，

sentences.en: those patterns vary depending upon whether they won or lost,
sentences.zh: 这些模式会根据胜负而变化，

sentences.en: but they did not vary across any of the countries or cultures that the athletes came from.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不因运动员来自的国家或文化而异。

sentences.en: Now, most laypeople would not necessarily be surprised by this.
sentences.zh: 现在，大多数外行未必会对此感到惊讶。

sentences.en: They would sort of say, yeah, sure, people win.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会说，是啊，当然，人们赢了，

sentences.en: They sort of look the same.
sentences.zh: 看起来都差不多。

sentences.en: But why is this interesting from a scientific perspective?
sentences.zh: 但从科学角度来看，为什么这很有趣呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting because actually before our study,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为实际上在我们的研究之前，

sentences.en: there were many, many studies that have shown that similar types of patterns of findings,
sentences.zh: 已经有许多研究表明了类似的发现模式，

sentences.en: cross-cultural similarities in these expressions.
sentences.zh: 即这些表情在跨文化中具有相似性。

sentences.en: But there was never a study that was done in what we call an ecologically valid environment
sentences.zh: 但从来没有一项研究是在我们所谓的“生态效度”环境中进行的，

sentences.en: out in the real world to show that people actually do this stuff in the real world
sentences.zh: 也就是在现实世界中，去证明人们在心理学实验室之外，

sentences.en: outside of a psychology laboratory.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中确实会有这种表现。

sentences.en: And I was just very, very fortunate to be able to do this study at the Olympics,
sentences.zh: 我非常非常幸运能在奥运会上进行这项研究，

sentences.en: which is a perfect social-psychological laboratory.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完美的社会心理学实验室。

sentences.en: In some ways, the study was basically making the argument, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这项研究基本上是在论证，我想，

sentences.en: that at least in the moment of triumph,
sentences.zh: 至少在胜利的瞬间，

sentences.en: people's reactions were shaped by what seemed like biologically innate imperatives.
sentences.zh: 人们的反应是由看似生物学上与生俱来的本能所塑造的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: However, that study by itself fell a little short.
sentences.zh: 然而，那项研究本身还有些不足。

sentences.en: So in actuality, we had the second study, which studied the Paralympic athletes.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们进行了第二项研究，研究了残奥会运动员。

sentences.en: And every sport in the Paralympics has a different disability.
sentences.zh: 残奥会中的每一项运动都有不同的残疾类别。

sentences.en: For judo, it's blindness.
sentences.zh: 对于柔道来说，是失明。

sentences.en: And so we compared the expressions of the blind athletes to those of the sighted athletes,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将盲人运动员与视力正常的运动员的表情进行了比较，

sentences.en: and we found exactly the same things.
sentences.zh: 结果我们发现了完全相同的东西。

sentences.en: So these are athletes who have been blind, some of them presumably blind from birth.
sentences.zh: 所以这些运动员一直失明，有些人大概是先天失明。

sentences.en: They presumably haven't really...
sentences.zh: 他们大概并没有真正……

sentences.en: Let's make it even clearer than that.
sentences.zh: 让我们说得更清楚一点。

sentences.en: We have athletes who are congenitally blind, so blind from birth.
sentences.zh: 我们研究的运动员是先天失明的，也就是从出生起就失明。

sentences.en: There's no presumption about what they've seen.
sentences.zh: 对于他们看过什么，不存在任何假设。

sentences.en: They've been impossible to see those expressions.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不可能看到过那些表情。

sentences.en: And the fact that they produce the same things on their faces for certain emotions,
sentences.zh: 而他们对于某些情绪在脸上产生相同的表情，

sentences.en: and then their bodies for triumph,
sentences.zh: 以及在胜利时身体表现出的反应，

sentences.en: absolutely suggests that these things are biologically innate.
sentences.zh: 绝对表明这些东西是生物学上与生俱来的。

sentences.en: What did the facial expression of triumph look like?
sentences.zh: 胜利的表情是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, triumph is actually a whole body response.
sentences.zh: 嗯，胜利实际上是一种全身性的反应。

sentences.en: It involves the expansion of the chest, raising the hands, oftentimes with a fist,
sentences.zh: 它包括挺胸、举手，通常还会握拳，

sentences.en: a little bit of fierce or aggressive look in the face,
sentences.zh: 脸上带着一点凶猛或好胜的神情，

sentences.en: and oftentimes a stern gaze at some kind of target.
sentences.zh: 而且通常会坚定地注视着某个目标。

sentences.en: Now, one of the things you found, which I found really fascinating, was,
sentences.zh: 现在，你发现的一件事让我觉得非常着迷，那就是，

sentences.en: yes, you do find evidence that some of these expressions are biologically innate,
sentences.zh: 是的，你确实发现了这些表情中有些是生物学上与生俱来的证据，

sentences.en: but you also find that culture plays a huge role at the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 但你也发现文化在奥运会上扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: Tell me about that part of the study.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说研究的那部分吧。

sentences.en: What we did was study the expressions across time.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是研究随时间变化的表情。

sentences.en: So even though we were using a camera, we were using a camera that was shooting eight photographs a second.
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们使用的是相机，我们使用的相机每秒能拍摄八张照片。

sentences.en: And so across a number of seconds, we can see how expressions transform across time.
sentences.zh: 因此，在几秒钟的时间里，我们可以看到表情是如何随时间转化的。

sentences.en: So immediately when a match ends, the winners and losers do something.
sentences.zh: 所以比赛一结束，胜者和败者就会做出某种反应。

sentences.en: That's immediate, automatic, it's unconscious, they have no control of it, it just happens.
sentences.zh: 那是即时的、自动的、无意识的，他们无法控制，它就这样发生了。

sentences.en: About a second later, then they come to their senses and they realize that they're on stage.
sentences.zh: 大约一秒钟后，他们回过神来，意识到自己正处于聚光灯下。

sentences.en: And whatever rules they've learned to manage their expressions kick in then.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们学会的那些用来管理表情的规则便开始发挥作用。

sentences.en: And that's that second expression or third expression sometimes where you see these vast cultural differences.
sentences.zh: 那就是第二种或有时是第三种表情，在那里你可以看到巨大的文化差异。

sentences.en: Some athletes are smiling, some athletes show nothing.
sentences.zh: 有些运动员在微笑，有些运动员毫无表情。

sentences.en: Some athletes start crying, some athletes do something else.
sentences.zh: 有些运动员开始哭泣，有些运动员做着其他动作。

sentences.en: But it's very interesting how you see the change at that point, but cultural invariance at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你在那一刻看到了变化，而最初却具有文化不变性。

sentences.en: You find that even though you have this range of emotions that kicks in after the first second or the first couple of seconds,
sentences.zh: 你发现，尽管在第一秒或前几秒之后会出现一系列情绪，

sentences.en: these are not random.
sentences.zh: 这些情绪并非随机的。

sentences.en: These actually are in some ways culturally determined,
sentences.zh: 它们在某种程度上实际上是受文化决定的，

sentences.en: that you actually find athletes from certain countries behave predictably differently than athletes from other countries.
sentences.zh: 你确实会发现来自某些国家的运动员的行为与来自其他国家的运动员有可预测的差异。

sentences.en: Yes, we were able to identify the various patterns of that cultural variation later on.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们后来能够识别出这种文化差异的各种模式。

sentences.en: So there are the neutralizers, those who kind of show nothing as stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 所以有“中和者”，那些表现得像刻板印象一样毫无表情的人。

sentences.en: You can think of Eastern Soviet bloc or old Soviet bloc countries, Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 你可以想到东欧苏联集团或旧苏联集团国家。

sentences.en: Those who have some communist history in them, Cuba, for example, are like that.
sentences.zh: 那些有共产主义历史的国家，比如古巴，就是这样。

sentences.en: You can think of the de-amplifiers, those who show something but it's muted a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你可以想到“减弱者”，那些表现出某种情绪但稍微克制一点的人。

sentences.en: There are a lot of North American, Western kind of cultures that do that.
sentences.zh: 很多北美、西方文化背景的人会这样做。

sentences.en: But there's those that smile a lot after something, even those that have something negative.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些人在某事发生后会微笑，即使是负面事件。

sentences.en: You can think of the East Asians as something like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以想到东亚人就是这样。

sentences.en: So yes, there are these very interesting cultural geographic variations
sentences.zh: 所以是的，在文化调节的主要模式如何运作方面，

sentences.en: on how the major patterns go in the cultural regulation.
sentences.zh: 存在着这些非常有趣的文化地理差异。

sentences.en: So in other words, people express what really maybe is happening inside them,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，人们表达了内心真实的想法，

sentences.en: but then the culture kicks in and says, here's the way you ought to behave in this situation.
sentences.zh: 但随后文化介入并说，在这种情况下你应该这样表现。

sentences.en: Yes, that's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: And the reason why most of us don't see that immediate reaction is because when something happens,
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人之所以看不到那种即时反应，是因为当事情发生时，

sentences.en: we're often looking at the thing that happened.
sentences.zh: 我们通常在看发生的事情本身。

sentences.en: So by the time we look at the person who it happened to, they're already on the cultural regulation part.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们看向当事人时，他们已经进入了文化调节阶段。

sentences.en: And it's people like us who have a camera on that person all the time
sentences.zh: 而像我们这样一直用相机对着那个人的人，

sentences.en: who are watching the immediate reactions so we can get the immediate reaction.
sentences.zh: 才能观察到即时反应，从而捕捉到那一刻。

sentences.en: One of the most celebrated studies looking at the Olympics, we featured it elsewhere on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 关于奥运会最著名的研究之一，我们曾在《隐藏的大脑》其他节目中介绍过。

sentences.en: This is a study by Thomas Gilovich at Cornell, along with Victoria Medvec and Scott Mady.
sentences.zh: 这是康奈尔大学的托马斯·吉洛维奇与维多利亚·梅德韦克和斯科特·马迪共同进行的一项研究。

sentences.en: He analyzed the expressions on the faces of medal winners in the Barcelona Olympics,
sentences.zh: 他分析了巴塞罗那奥运会奖牌获得者的面部表情，

sentences.en: and he found that in general, bronze medal winners looked happier than silver medal winners.
sentences.zh: 他发现总的来说，铜牌获得者看起来比银牌获得者更快乐。

sentences.en: I'm going to let you tell me why that might be the case,
sentences.zh: 我让你来告诉我为什么会这样，

sentences.en: but also how your own research both amplified and has a nuance to that finding.
sentences.zh: 同时也谈谈你自己的研究是如何既扩展了这一发现，又为其增添了细微差别。

sentences.en: Well, we found exactly the same things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们发现了完全相同的结果。

sentences.en: Actually, one of the great things about our study is that not only were we able to study the expressions of the athletes
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们研究的一大优点是，我们不仅能够研究运动员的表情，

sentences.en: right when they won a loss, right when they're on the mat,
sentences.zh: 就在他们胜负已分、就在赛场上的时候，

sentences.en: we could follow them 30 minutes later in the medal ceremony.
sentences.zh: 我们还能在30分钟后的颁奖仪式上跟踪他们。

sentences.en: So we saw what the same person did who had the same result, but it's now the social context is different.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了同一个人在结果相同的情况下做了什么，但现在的社会背景不同了。

sentences.en: And you're exactly right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: The silver medalists, everybody on the podium smiles.
sentences.zh: 银牌得主，领奖台上的每个人都会微笑。

sentences.en: So there's no question about it because this is a very public televised thing.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问，因为这是一个非常公开的电视转播场合。

sentences.en: But if you measure the exact muscles that are moving in the smiles, you'll find that,
sentences.zh: 但如果你测量微笑时移动的确切肌肉，你会发现，

sentences.en: let's call the silver medal smiles more of the miserable smile because they've got a lot of other things going on.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把银牌得主的微笑称为“痛苦的微笑”，因为他们内心还有很多其他情绪。

sentences.en: You won't see the crinkle in the eyes.
sentences.zh: 你不会看到眼角的皱纹。

sentences.en: Sometimes you'll see the downturning of the lips because they're really trying to control some negative feelings along with a smile.
sentences.zh: 有时你会看到嘴角下垂，因为他们真的在努力控制一些负面情绪，同时还要保持微笑。

sentences.en: So some of them look miserable when they're smiling.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人微笑时看起来很痛苦。

sentences.en: And Gilevich would argue this is because the silver medal winners are comparing themselves to the gold medal winners
sentences.zh: 吉洛维奇会认为这是因为银牌得主在拿自己和金牌得主做比较，

sentences.en: and saying if I only had gone half a second faster, if I'd only jumped a little bit faster, I could be a gold medal winner.
sentences.zh: 心想如果我再快半秒，如果我再跳得快一点，我可能就是金牌得主了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so when you get to the bronze medalists, they have more reason to be happier because the alternative is nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到铜牌得主时，他们有更多理由感到快乐，因为另一种选择是空手而归。

sentences.en: Whereas the silver medalists, the alternative was the gold.
sentences.zh: 而银牌得主，另一种选择是金牌。

sentences.en: And so in our study, we also found that the bronze medalists had more of the enjoyment smiles than the silver medalists did.
sentences.zh: 因此在我们的研究中，我们也发现铜牌得主比银牌得主有更多的愉悦微笑。

sentences.en: The only exceptions that we found to this bronze medalist thing that I thought was really interesting,
sentences.zh: 关于铜牌得主，我发现唯一有趣的例外是，

sentences.en: when I look back at our data, there are some bronze medalists who did not look very happy.
sentences.zh: 当我回顾我们的数据时，有些铜牌得主看起来并不怎么高兴。

sentences.en: And these were generally the winners of the world championships of the previous year who came into the Olympics as the favorite,
sentences.zh: 这些人通常是前一年世界锦标赛的冠军，作为夺冠热门来到奥运会，

sentences.en: and they had to settle for a bronze.
sentences.zh: 结果却只能屈居铜牌。

sentences.en: So because they had to settle for a bronze, they were not as happy as those who are getting a bronze.
sentences.zh: 所以因为他们不得不满足于铜牌，他们并不像那些获得铜牌的人那样高兴。

sentences.en: And, you know, a lot of them didn't expect to get a medal or they were just happy to get a medal.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们中的许多人并没有期望获得奖牌，或者他们只是很高兴能拿到奖牌。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask David about his own experience at the Olympics
sentences.zh: 回来后，我要问问戴维他在奥运会上的亲身经历。

sentences.en: and what a psychologist might learn from being a coach and being a parent of an Olympia.
sentences.zh: 以及心理学家能从担任教练和奥运选手家长的经历中学到什么。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Support for Hidden Brain and the following message come from First Republic Bank.

sentences.en: Interesting fact about First Republic.
sentences.zh: 关于第一共和银行的一个有趣事实。

sentences.en: First Republic is a bank with no teller lines,
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行是一家没有柜台排队的银行，

sentences.en: but they didn't replace their tellers with computers or robots.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有用电脑或机器人取代柜员。

sentences.en: How is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能呢？

sentences.en: Personal bankers.
sentences.zh: 私人银行家。

sentences.en: Every client has their own personal banker, and bankers know all their clients.
sentences.zh: 每位客户都有自己的私人银行家，而且银行家了解他们所有的客户。

sentences.en: First Republic has a personal approach to banking,
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行采用个性化的银行服务方式，

sentences.en: and they're dedicated to providing extraordinary service.
sentences.zh: 他们致力于提供非凡的服务。

sentences.en: Visit firstrepublic.com to hear from their clients.
sentences.zh: 请访问 firstrepublic.com 听听他们客户的评价。

sentences.en: First Republic.
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行。

sentences.en: It's a privilege to serve you.
sentences.zh: 为您服务是我们的荣幸。

sentences.en: Support also comes from LearnVeSt.
sentences.zh: 节目支持也来自 LearnVest。

sentences.en: LearnVest is an online financial advice company focused on empowering people nationwide
sentences.zh: LearnVest 是一家在线理财咨询公司，专注于赋能全国人民，

sentences.en: to make good decisions with their money.
sentences.zh: 帮助他们做出明智的财务决策。

sentences.en: Studies show that writing down your goals makes you 49% more likely to achieve them.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，写下你的目标能让你实现目标的可能性提高 49%。

sentences.en: That's why when you work with LearnVest, you tell them what you want to accomplish,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当你与 LearnVest 合作时，你告诉他们你想实现什么，

sentences.en: and they create a customized financial plan to help you get there.
sentences.zh: 他们会为你制定个性化的财务计划来帮助你达成目标。

sentences.en: Plus, they pair you with a financial planner to help keep you on track.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们还会为你匹配一名理财规划师，帮助你保持进度。

sentences.en: To see a sample plan and get a $50 credit, go to learnveSt.com slash brain.
sentences.zh: 要查看计划样本并获得 50 美元的抵用金，请访问 learnvest.com/brain。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Chris Benderev, one of the producers of Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是 Chris Benderev，Hidden Brain 的制作人之一。

sentences.en: Here's a great way to listen to our show, NPR One.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个收听我们节目的好方法：NPR One。

sentences.en: It's an app for your phone, kind of like Pandora, but for public radio.
sentences.zh: 这是一款手机应用，有点像 Pandora，但它是专门针对公共广播的。

sentences.en: It's full of news and stories from your favorite podcasters, NPR,
sentences.zh: 它汇集了你最喜欢的播客、NPR 的新闻和故事，

sentences.en: and the local station that you call your own.
sentences.zh: 以及你所熟悉的当地电台。

sentences.en: Whenever you're ready to listen, NPR One has something great just for you.
sentences.zh: 无论你何时想听，NPR One 总有适合你的精彩内容。

sentences.en: All right, now back to Shankar's interview with psychology professor David Matsumoto
sentences.zh: 好了，现在回到 Shankar 对心理学教授 David Matsumoto 的采访，

sentences.en: on the science behind Olympic athletes.
sentences.zh: 探讨奥运选手背后的科学。

sentences.en: Give me some sense of the scale of what's happening in an athlete on the judo mat in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 请让我了解一下奥运会柔道赛场上运动员身上所发生变化的程度。

sentences.en: I mean, physiologically, what's happening to them?
sentences.zh: 我是说，从生理学角度来看，他们身上发生了什么？

sentences.en: I'll tell you exactly what's happening because we've actually studied this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉你到底发生了什么，因为我们确实研究过这类事情。

sentences.en: You know, if you and I are sitting down here right now having this conversation,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们俩现在坐在这里交谈，

sentences.en: if we clocked our heart rate, if we're healthy and normal,
sentences.zh: 如果我们测量心率，假设我们身体健康正常，

sentences.en: we'd probably be about 60, 72, something like that.
sentences.zh: 心率大概会在 60 到 72 次左右。

sentences.en: Since we're doing something that's really exciting right now,
sentences.zh: 因为我们现在正在做一件非常令人兴奋的事情，

sentences.en: maybe we're at 80 or something.
sentences.zh: 也许心率会达到 80 左右。

sentences.en: If you imagine yourself taking a jog, you might be at 70% of your max heart rate,
sentences.zh: 如果你想象自己在慢跑，心率可能会达到最大心率的 70%，

sentences.en: which would maybe be at 130, 140, depending upon your age.
sentences.zh: 根据年龄不同，可能在 130 或 140 左右。

sentences.en: In a judo match, we've actually clocked athletes' heart rates around 200 beats a minute.
sentences.zh: 在柔道比赛中，我们实际测得运动员的心率约为每分钟 200 次。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And these are highly conditioned athletes.
sentences.zh: 而且这些都是经过高度训练的运动员。

sentences.en: You've got to be highly conditioned to be at 200 beats a minute.
sentences.zh: 你必须经过高度训练才能达到每分钟 200 次心率。

sentences.en: And this is 200 beats a minute in combat conditions.
sentences.zh: 而且这是在战斗状态下每分钟 200 次心率。

sentences.en: Now, think about what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 现在，想想我所说的话。

sentences.en: You're going to be at 200 beats a minute in combat conditions,
sentences.zh: 你将在战斗状态下达到每分钟 200 次心率，

sentences.en: thinking clearly, being on your game,
sentences.zh: 同时还要保持思维清晰，发挥出水平，

sentences.en: knowing exactly what you're doing technically, strategically, and everything else.
sentences.zh: 在技术、战略和其他各方面都清楚自己到底在做什么。

sentences.en: To get to that point, it's not easy.
sentences.zh: 要达到那种程度，并不容易。

sentences.en: It's nothing that we can sit around and talk about.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们坐下来聊聊就能做到的。

sentences.en: It's nothing that I can really sit here and kind of help you like a traditional psychologist would.
sentences.zh: 这也不是我作为传统心理学家坐在这里就能帮你解决的。

sentences.en: To tell you the truth, I've got to get you to be really physical.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我必须让你进行高强度的身体训练。

sentences.en: And I've got to train your body to tolerate the lactic acid that your body generates
sentences.zh: 我必须训练你的身体去耐受身体产生的乳酸，

sentences.en: as I get you to that profile.
sentences.zh: 从而让你达到那种状态。

sentences.en: How do you get athletes as a coach to actually keep thinking
sentences.zh: 作为教练，你如何让运动员在身体处于高度亢奋状态时，

sentences.en: when their bodies are in the state of hyperarousal?
sentences.zh: 依然保持思考？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, you have to get them to be used to that state of hyperarousal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，你必须让他们习惯那种高度亢奋的状态。

sentences.en: So there's a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要很长一段时间。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking, it'll take several years of what we call periodized training
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们谈论的是需要几年我们所谓的周期性训练，

sentences.en: to get an athlete to be at peak physical condition.
sentences.zh: 才能让运动员达到巅峰身体状态。

sentences.en: Once you're there or along the way you're there,
sentences.zh: 一旦你达到了那个状态，或者在达到那个状态的过程中，

sentences.en: what you can do is then add in some drills, cognitive drills,
sentences.zh: 你可以加入一些训练，认知训练，

sentences.en: for athletes to do once they're at that level.
sentences.zh: 让运动员在达到那个水平后进行练习。

sentences.en: So for example, I can create a situation where I'll get an athlete's heart rate up to 200.
sentences.zh: 例如，我可以创造一种情况，让运动员的心率达到 200 次。

sentences.en: You know, it's not easy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不容易。

sentences.en: It's not fun.
sentences.zh: 这并不好玩。

sentences.en: You don't want to be that person.
sentences.zh: 你不会想成为那样的人。

sentences.en: But once you're there, I can have you do a crossword puzzle, right?
sentences.zh: 但一旦你到了那个状态，我可以让你做填字游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: One of the things that we used to do is we used to have people run around a track,
sentences.zh: 我们过去常做的一件事是让人们绕着跑道跑，

sentences.en: sprinting the 800 meters around the track.
sentences.zh: 绕着跑道冲刺 800 米。

sentences.en: And once they come off the track, untie these humongous ropes with knots in them,
sentences.zh: 当他们跑完跑道后，去解开那些打着结的巨大绳子，

sentences.en: which is entirely frustrating to do.
sentences.zh: 这做起来非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: But, you know, you got to deal with the frustration when your heart is going at 200 beats a minute
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当你的心率达到每分钟 200 次时，你必须应对这种挫败感，

sentences.en: to do this little complex cognition task.
sentences.zh: 去完成这个小小的复杂认知任务。

sentences.en: One of the things that I find so fascinating is that so much of the Olympics actually happens
sentences.zh: 我发现最迷人的一点是，奥运会的很多事情实际上都发生在

sentences.en: out of sight of the TV cameras.
sentences.zh: 电视摄像机看不到的地方。

sentences.en: So athletes have to get ready.
sentences.zh: 所以运动员必须做好准备。

sentences.en: They have to warm up.
sentences.zh: 他们必须热身。

sentences.en: In fact, just getting to your competition itself can be a struggle,
sentences.zh: 事实上，仅仅是到达比赛现场本身就是一种挣扎，

sentences.en: especially if you're competing on day one.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你在第一天就要比赛的话。

sentences.en: Well, you're exactly right, because most of the public who watch these sports,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得完全正确，因为大多数观看这些运动的公众，

sentences.en: who are great, by the way, we wouldn't be here without our fans,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们都很棒，没有粉丝我们就不可能站在这里，

sentences.en: but most of the public just turns on the TV and can see this peak performance.
sentences.zh: 但大多数公众只是打开电视，看到的是巅峰表现。

sentences.en: And competition really is maybe the third thing that the athletes are worrying about.
sentences.zh: 而比赛实际上可能是运动员担心的第三件事。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the main thing, but it's always the third thing.
sentences.zh: 也许它是最重要的事情，但它总是排在第三位。

sentences.en: The first thing that we're always worrying about, number one, is making weight.
sentences.zh: 我们最担心的第一件事，第一位，是控制体重。

sentences.en: Because in judo, you've got a weight division.
sentences.zh: 因为在柔道中，有体重级别限制。

sentences.en: And everyone is, we call it walking around weight.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有所谓的日常体重。

sentences.en: Everyone's walking around weight is heavier than what their weight division is.
sentences.zh: 每个人的日常体重都比他们的比赛级别要重。

sentences.en: So you've got to be on a program to cut down to a certain amount right before you're weighing in.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须制定一个计划，在称重前减掉一定的重量。

sentences.en: And then everyone's got a routine to cut to weigh in.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有自己的减重流程。

sentences.en: And it's not fun cutting weight.
sentences.zh: 减重可不好玩。

sentences.en: And it's not fun being with 20 people who are starving themselves.
sentences.zh: 和 20 个正在挨饿的人待在一起也不好玩。

sentences.en: And if you have to be in starvation mode for a week, 10 days, whatever that is,
sentences.zh: 如果你必须处于饥饿模式一周、10 天，无论多久，

sentences.en: it's a miserable experience.
sentences.zh: 那都是一种痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: Now, some people do that better than others,
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人比其他人做得更好，

sentences.en: but it's not the thing that you think that you'd want to be doing with your life most of the time.
sentences.zh: 但这不是你大部分时间想在生活中做的事情。

sentences.en: So that's the first thing that the athlete's thinking about.
sentences.zh: 所以这是运动员考虑的第一件事。

sentences.en: What's the second?
sentences.zh: 第二件事是什么？

sentences.en: The second thing is the jet lag.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是时差。

sentences.en: So the Olympics are in Rio.
sentences.zh: 奥运会在里约举行。

sentences.en: And if you're coming from where I live, which is San Francisco, you're four hours away.
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样住在旧金山，你离那里有四个小时的时差。

sentences.en: And so you have to think about the four-hour difference.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须考虑这四个小时的差异。

sentences.en: If the Olympics were in Athens, like they were in 2004, now we're talking about a 10-hour difference.
sentences.zh: 如果奥运会在雅典举行，就像 2004 年那样，那就有 10 个小时的差异了。

sentences.en: Olympics are going to be in Tokyo in 2020.
sentences.zh: 2020 年奥运会将在东京举行。

sentences.en: Now we're talking about a nine-hour difference the other way if you're in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 如果你在旧金山，那就有 9 个小时的时差了。

sentences.en: And these are big differences because if you're talking about peak performance,
sentences.zh: 这些差异很大，因为如果你谈论的是巅峰表现，

sentences.en: you want people to be rested well, fed well, in peak mental condition.
sentences.zh: 你希望人们休息好、吃得好，处于巅峰心理状态。

sentences.en: And it's especially difficult if you're competing on day one and you want to be in the opening ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 如果你在第一天就要比赛，又想参加开幕式，那就特别困难。

sentences.en: And the thing that people don't know about the opening ceremonies is it usually ends around midnight,
sentences.zh: 人们不知道的一点是，开幕式通常在午夜左右结束，

sentences.en: wherever the host country is.
sentences.zh: 无论是在哪个主办国。

sentences.en: And everyone's got to get on a bus that the local committee sets up.
sentences.zh: 每个人都得坐上当地组委会安排的巴士。

sentences.en: And it's just chaos.
sentences.zh: 那简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: It's just the zoo.
sentences.zh: 简直就像个动物园。

sentences.en: So many athletes get loSt.
sentences.zh: 很多运动员都会迷路。

sentences.en: Buses don't know where to go.
sentences.zh: 巴士司机不知道该去哪里。

sentences.en: And so you might get on your bus at 12 o'clock and you might be back in the village at 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能 12 点上了巴士，回到村里可能已经是凌晨 3 点了，

sentences.en: and you might have a 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 而你可能早上 6 点

sentences.en: weigh-in time.
sentences.zh: 就要称重。

sentences.en: And so obviously if you did that, it kind of screws you up for that competition.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，如果你那样做了，那会对你的比赛产生负面影响。

sentences.en: It turns out that flying east and flying west to get to the Games is not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，向东飞和向西飞去参加比赛是不一样的。

sentences.en: That in some ways it's better for the human body if you happen to be flying in one direction rather than the other.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，如果你恰好朝着一个方向飞行，对人体来说会更好。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In fact, it's easier to go in one direction rather than another
sentences.zh: 事实上，朝一个方向飞比朝另一个方向飞更容易，

sentences.en: because our bodies are built to function better on a 25-hour cycle than a 24-hour cycle.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的身体在 25 小时的周期内比在 24 小时的周期内运作得更好。

sentences.en: That's why it's easier for us to stay up longer than it is to get up earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们熬夜比早起更容易。

sentences.en: And how that translates to travel is when we travel west, our time zones are getting later.
sentences.zh: 这转化为旅行就是，当我们向西旅行时，时区会变晚。

sentences.en: You just have to stay up a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 你只需要晚一点睡。

sentences.en: We just have to stay up a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要晚一点睡。

sentences.en: And that's easier.
sentences.zh: 这更容易。

sentences.en: When we travel east, like I came from San Francisco and here I am in D.C.
sentences.zh: 当我们向东旅行时，比如我从旧金山来到这里，现在在华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: now, that's a three-hour time zone.
sentences.zh: 现在有三个小时的时差。

sentences.en: So this morning I had to be at a certain place at 7 o'clock, which is 4 o'clock my time,
sentences.zh: 所以今天早上我必须在 7 点钟到达某个地方，那是我时间的 4 点钟，

sentences.en: which means I had to get up at 3 o'clock my time, which is more difficult.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我必须在我时间的 3 点钟起床，这更困难。

sentences.en: So, yes, we take these kinds of factors into account.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们会把这些因素考虑在内。

sentences.en: You know, I think when people think about the Olympics who haven't been there, it seems very glamorous, very fun.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为当没去过奥运会的人想到奥运会时，它看起来非常迷人，非常有趣。

sentences.en: You know, you're on this world stage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你站在这个世界舞台上。

sentences.en: Everyone's watching you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在看着你。

sentences.en: Everyone's cheering for you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在为你欢呼。

sentences.en: Everyone's hoping that you do well.
sentences.zh: 每个人都希望你表现出色。

sentences.en: And they clap for you when you succeed.
sentences.zh: 当你成功时，他们为你鼓掌。

sentences.en: And you're at peak performance.
sentences.zh: 你处于巅峰表现状态。

sentences.en: And it seems like it's sort of a glorious time in your life and the life of, you know, the coaching staff and so on.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是你生命中以及教练团队等人的生命中一段光荣的时光。

sentences.en: Is that how it actually feels when you're there?
sentences.zh: 当你身处其中时，感觉真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, I can't speak for everybody else.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不能代表其他人发言。

sentences.en: I got to say that I never felt that glorious times in the four Olympics and the 12 world championships that I've been to.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，在我参加过的四届奥运会和 12 届世锦赛中，我从未感到过那种光荣时刻。

sentences.en: Because as a coaching staff member, first of all, you're not done with your feelings until everyone's done competing.
sentences.zh: 因为作为教练组成员，首先，在每个人比赛结束之前，你的心情都不会放松。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I never had the situation where everyone on my team got a gold medal.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我从未遇到过团队中每个人都获得金牌的情况。

sentences.en: And if that happened, then I think after the competition, everything is glorious.
sentences.zh: 如果发生了那种情况，那么我想比赛结束后，一切都是光荣的。

sentences.en: But no matter how good our team did, whether it's my local team or the Olympic team or whatever teams we're talking about,
sentences.zh: 但无论我们的团队表现得多么出色，无论是我的地方队、奥运代表队，还是我们谈论的任何团队，

sentences.en: if there's one person that didn't make it, you know, if there's one person that didn't get what they wanted, I felt it.
sentences.zh: 只要有一个人没能成功，你知道，只要有一个人没能如愿以偿，我都能感同身受。

sentences.en: I could have nine players take a gold and if one person took a silver, of course I'm happy.
sentences.zh: 我可以有九名选手拿到金牌，如果有一个人拿了银牌，我当然会为他高兴。

sentences.en: But it lingers for me.
sentences.zh: 但那种遗憾会萦绕在我心头。

sentences.en: I think that's true for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都是这样。

sentences.en: And I'll give you a good example of this.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个很好的例子。

sentences.en: When my daughter made the Olympic team in 2008, at the Olympic trials, her competitor in the finals was another woman from my dojo.
sentences.zh: 2008年我女儿入选奥运代表队时，在奥运选拔赛的决赛中，她的对手是我道场里的另一位选手。

sentences.en: And so as a judo instructor, you have two of your players in the finals of the Olympic trials.
sentences.zh: 作为柔道教练，你的两名选手同时进入了奥运选拔赛的决赛。

sentences.en: You know you're golden because no matter who wins, someone from your dojo is going to go and be on the Olympic team.
sentences.zh: 你知道你稳操胜券了，因为无论谁赢，你道场里的人都会去参加奥运会。

sentences.en: But one of the competitors is your daughter.
sentences.zh: 但其中一名选手是你女儿。

sentences.en: One of them is my daughter and the other one is my student who I treat like a daughter.
sentences.zh: 一个是我的女儿，另一个是我视如己出的学生。

sentences.en: And on top of that, when we're in competition, I don't have a daughter.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，在比赛期间，我没有女儿。

sentences.en: I have a player.
sentences.zh: 我只有一名选手。

sentences.en: You know, and my daughter knew that and we all knew that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我女儿明白这一点，我们也都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And I treated my daughter like anybody else in competition.
sentences.zh: 在比赛中，我对待我女儿就像对待其他人一样。

sentences.en: Now, after competition, you know, she's my daughter.
sentences.zh: 当然，比赛结束后，她就是我的女儿。

sentences.en: But when we're in competition, she's another player and I got to treat her like I treat everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但在比赛时，她就是另一名选手，我必须像对待其他人一样对待她。

sentences.en: And so anyway, we have these two players coming up.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们有这两名选手要上场。

sentences.en: And I have mixed feelings about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此心情很复杂。

sentences.en: You know, when my daughter won, I was happy for her.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我女儿赢的时候，我为她感到高兴。

sentences.en: But I was very sad for my other player who loSt.
sentences.zh: 但我为输掉比赛的另一名选手感到非常难过。

sentences.en: So after that, it was a very bittersweet thing to have occurred.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后，发生的一切真是苦乐参半。

sentences.en: And yeah, I mean, I don't want to take anything from my daughter as a parent.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，作为父母，我不想从我女儿身上夺走任何东西。

sentences.en: If I could compartmentalize my feeling as solely as a parent, yeah, great.
sentences.zh: 如果我能仅仅以父母的身份来处理我的感受，那当然很好。

sentences.en: I'm happy.
sentences.zh: 我会很高兴。

sentences.en: But no one can compartmentalize 100% where I couldn't.
sentences.zh: 但没有人能百分之百地做到这一点，我也做不到。

sentences.en: And so as a parent, I felt good.
sentences.zh: 所以作为父母，我感觉很好。

sentences.en: As an instructor, I felt good and bad.
sentences.zh: 作为教练，我感觉既好又坏。

sentences.en: And it's mixed up feelings that one had.
sentences.zh: 那是一种混合的复杂感受。

sentences.en: And I still have it to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我依然有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I remember it very clearly right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在依然记忆犹新。

sentences.en: When you watch the Olympics now, and let's say you're not at the Olympics, let's say you're not going to – are you going to Rio?
sentences.zh: 当你现在观看奥运会时，假设你不在奥运会现场，假设你不会去——你会去里约吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不去。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So when you watch the Olympics on television now, what is it that you're watching?
sentences.zh: 那么当你现在在电视上观看奥运会时，你到底在看什么？

sentences.en: What is it that you pay attention to, knowing all that you know as a psychologist who studied the Olympics, as a coach who's coached at the Olympics, as a parent at the Olympics?
sentences.zh: 作为一个研究过奥运会的心理学家，一个在奥运会上执教过的教练，一个在奥运会现场的家长，你了解这一切，那么你关注的是什么？

sentences.en: What do you look for now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在寻找什么？

sentences.en: I look at a lot of things, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我关注很多事情。

sentences.en: And when I see peak performance of any type, it doesn't have to be sports, even when I look at dancers or somebody who's really good at doing something that's difficult to do,
sentences.zh: 当我看到任何形式的巅峰表现时，不一定是体育运动，即使是看舞蹈演员，或者看某人真正擅长做一些困难的事情时，

sentences.en: they make it look so easy.
sentences.zh: 他们让这一切看起来如此轻松。

sentences.en: And I automatically think about the sweat and the tears and the blood and the effort for years that that person put in to be able to do that, that we saw that was just effortless.
sentences.zh: 我自然而然地会想到那个人为了做到这一点，多年来付出的汗水、泪水、鲜血和努力，而我们看到的却只是毫不费力。

sentences.en: When you're at competition, you're talking about a few minutes, an hour of years of preparation.
sentences.zh: 当你身处赛场时，你看到的只是几分钟、一小时的比赛，背后却是多年的准备。

sentences.en: And you can't divorce your memories from those years of preparation.
sentences.zh: 你无法将你的记忆与那些年的准备工作剥离开来。

sentences.en: Those things overwhelm me, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些事情让我感慨万千。

sentences.en: And so when you're thinking about the athletes, you're actually thinking about all of those, the times that we're not seeing on television,
sentences.zh: 所以当你想到运动员时，你实际上想到的是所有那些我们在电视上看不到的时刻，

sentences.en: all of the waking up at four o'clock in the morning and practicing on the weekends and giving up other aspects of your life.
sentences.zh: 所有那些凌晨四点起床、周末练习以及放弃生活中其他方面的时刻。

sentences.en: And not just for the people who win, but also for everybody else who's there.
sentences.zh: 不仅是为了那些获胜的人，也是为了所有在那里参赛的其他人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone's made a huge sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人都做出了巨大的牺牲。

sentences.en: And of course, the player or the athlete is always the number one sacrificer.
sentences.zh: 当然，选手或运动员永远是头号牺牲者。

sentences.en: But think about all their support staff.
sentences.zh: 但想想他们所有的后勤支持人员。

sentences.en: For us, for every player that we had on the mat, we had a support team of 10 or 20 just to get that person on the mat.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，赛场上的每一名选手背后，都有一个10到20人的支持团队，只为了让那个人能站在赛场上。

sentences.en: And so behind one person, there's an army.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个人身后是一支军队。

sentences.en: And everyone's on the same team.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在同一个团队里。

sentences.en: And they never share the limelight.
sentences.zh: 他们从不分享聚光灯。

sentences.en: They never get the spotlight.
sentences.zh: 他们从不站在镁光灯下。

sentences.en: They just share in the knowledge that they help this person have a peak performance.
sentences.zh: 他们只是分享着这份认知：他们帮助这个人实现了巅峰表现。

sentences.en: And when that person wins, everyone feels good.
sentences.zh: 当那个人获胜时，每个人都感到高兴。

sentences.en: And when that person loses, everyone feels awful.
sentences.zh: 当那个人失败时，每个人都感到难过。

sentences.en: And it's all those people, as well as the athletes, that my heart actually reaches out to when I see these things.
sentences.zh: 当我看到这些事情时，我的心不仅牵挂着运动员，也牵挂着所有这些人。

sentences.en: David Matsumoto, I want to thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 大卫·松本，感谢你今天参加《Hidden Brain》节目。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
